summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex history including fibrosing mesenteritis, multiple abdominal surgeries, chronic TPN dependence, and recurrent line infections was admitted due to a positive blood culture for coagulase-negative staphylococcus from her PICC line. She remained clinically stable without fever or systemic signs of infection. The PICC line was removed, and subsequent cultures from the line tip and repeated blood draws were negative. Multiple attempts to place a new upper extremity central line failed due to venous stenoses and a non-occlusive thrombus in the right subclavian vein. A tunneled left femoral double-lumen central line was successfully placed for ongoing TPN. Infectious disease recommended further molecular testing to evaluate for a persistent source. The patient was discharged home with home health services to manage her line and nutrition, with follow-up arranged with her ID and GI specialists.
problems: Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
